candidates.locator: page 8, section part_i, B. 24-HOUR ORAL REPORTING: DAILY MAXIMUM LIMITATION VIOLATIONS
candidates.exact_span: Under the provisions of Part III.D.7.b.(3) of this permit, violations of daily maximum limitations for the following pollutants shall be reported orally to EPA Region 6, Compliance and Assurance Division, Water Enforcement Branch (6EN-W), Dallas, Texas, and concurrently to NMED within 24 hours from the time the permittee becomes aware of the violation followed by a written report in five days.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Cross-reference to Part III.D.7.b.(3) and the phrase 'daily maximum limitations' tie this reporting trigger to specific limit types and pollutants; different readings of what Part III.D.7.b.(3) establishes, or which pollutants are covered, could change which daily maximum limits are treated as operative and which violation-reporting obligations are in scope for FY2025.

candidates.locator: page 8, section part_i, B. 24-HOUR ORAL REPORTING: DAILY MAXIMUM LIMITATION VIOLATIONS
candidates.computation_change_reason: The empty pollutant list following 'for the following pollutants' is ambiguous: it may mean no pollutants are subject to 24-hour oral reporting for daily maximum violations, or it may be read alongside other text as indicating the absence or non-applicability of daily maximum limitations in this subsection; either reading could change which limits or reporting-linked obligations are evaluated.

candidates.locator: page 8, section part_i, D. WHOLE EFFLUENT TOXICITY TESTING (7 DAY CHRONIC NOEC)
candidates.exact_span: D. WHOLE EFFLUENT TOXICITY TESTING (7 DAY CHRONIC NOEC)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Introduces whole effluent toxicity as a permit compliance area with a 7-day chronic NOEC limit framework; interpretation of whether NOEC is an enforceable numeric limit versus a monitoring-only requirement affects limit applicability (A) and whether WET monitoring is obligatory (B).

candidates.locator: page 8, section part_i, D. WHOLE EFFLUENT TOXICITY TESTING, paragraph on sample manipulation and test completion
candidates.exact_span: It is unlawful and a violation of this permit for a permittee or his designated agent, to manipulate test samples in any manner, to delay sample shipment, or to terminate or to cause to terminate a toxicity test. Once initiated, all toxicity tests must be completed unless specific authority has been granted by EPA Region 6 or the State NPDES permitting authority.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a toxicity test was properly completed, terminated early, or compromised affects how missing or irregular WET results are classified—e.g., required monitoring lacking adequate evidence versus a documented no-data or not-required state.

candidates.locator: page 8, section part_i, D. WHOLE EFFLUENT TOXICITY TESTING, 1. SCOPE AND METHODOLOGY, a.
candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall test the effluent for toxicity in accordance with the provisions in this section.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes a mandatory WET monitoring obligation; interpretation of scope ('effluent', 'in accordance with the provisions in this section') determines whether WET monitoring was required for applicable outfalls and periods in FY2025.

candidates.locator: page 8, section part_i, D. WHOLE EFFLUENT TOXICITY TESTING, table row APPLICABLE TO FINAL OUTFALL(S)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Scopes WET limits and testing to Final Outfall 001; different readings of which outfalls qualify as 'final outfall(s) 001' change where WET limits apply (A) and where WET monitoring is required (B).

candidates.locator: page 8, section part_i, D. WHOLE EFFLUENT TOXICITY TESTING, table row CRITICAL DILUTION (%)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Critical dilution percentage is a methodological parameter for evaluating toxicity against the NOEC; a different interpreted value or application rule would change how reported WET results are compared to applicable limits.

candidates.locator: page 8, section part_i, D. WHOLE EFFLUENT TOXICITY TESTING, table row EFFLUENT DILUTION SERIES (%)
candidates.computation_change_reason: The prescribed dilution series governs how chronic toxicity is tested and how NOEC/pass-fail is derived; interpretation of which series applies or how it is used could change compliance determinations against WET limits.

candidates.locator: page 8, section part_i, D. WHOLE EFFLUENT TOXICITY TESTING, table row TEST SPECIES AND METHODS
candidates.exact_span:
TEST SPECIES AND METHODS           Ceriodaphnia dubia / Method 1002.0
                                      (EPA-821-R-02-013 or latest version)
                                      Pimephales promelas/ Method 1000.0
                                      (EPA/821/R-02-013 or latest version)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Required test species and method versions determine whether reported WET data are valid for limit comparison (A), whether monitoring met permit requirements (B), and whether absent or nonconforming results reflect missing required evidence versus an established no-data or not-applicable state (C).

candidates.locator: page 8, section part_i, D. WHOLE EFFLUENT TOXICITY TESTING, table row SAMPLE TYPE
candidates.exact_span: SAMPLE TYPE                        Defined in PART I
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sample type is defined only by cross-reference to PART I; resolving what PART I requires (grab vs. composite, timing, conditions) affects which WET samples are valid for limit comparison (A), when monitoring was required (B), and how to classify periods without conforming sample results (C).
